categories.name: Information
categories.definition: Adds factual or explanatory content about the video: sources, trivia, background, translations, timestamps, or explanations of what is on screen.

categories.name: Humor
categories.definition: A joke, pun, meme reference, or witty remark whose main purpose is to amuse, with some content beyond pure laughter.
examples: 这波操作属实是反向带货

categories.name: Emotional resonance
categories.definition: Expresses or echoes emotion, empathy, agreement, or shared feeling with the video or with other viewers.

categories.name: Irrelevant repetition
categories.definition: Low-information, repetitive, or spam-like reactions: character flooding, number or word spam, first, front row, passing by, empty hype.

categories.name: Attack
categories.definition: Insults, harassment, or hostility directed at a person or group: the creator, other viewers, or people in the video.

categories.name: Conflict
categories.definition: Argumentative or confrontational replies that escalate disagreement, including provocation and dismissive taunts, without an explicit insult.

categories.name: Spoiler
categories.definition: Reveals content that appears later in the video or story and ruins surprise; requires video context and a timestamp to judge.
examples: 剧透预警：他最后没活下来

categories.name: Political stance
categories.definition: States, implies, or mocks a political position on public affairs: policy, institutions, leaders, elections, or national, ethnic and regional identity. The stance can be serious or ironic.

categories.name: Inflammatory bait
categories.definition: Deliberately provokes or takes sides in a heated social issue (gender, region, fandom, morality) to start a fight or rally a camp, without necessarily insulting a specific person.

categories.name: Other / unclassifiable
categories.definition: Text whose social function cannot be judged from the text and timestamp, or that does not serve any function above: off-topic chatter, private inside references, raw symbol strings, or unreadable fragments.
categories.usage: Last resort, not a safe default. Label other only when every tag scores below 0.2; when a comment is merely ambiguous, give the closest tag a low score and explain the choice in the note.
